description: Fast, accurate OCR with correctness assessment.

summary.one_liner: MiniCPM-OCR is a family of OCR models from OpenBMB: MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 parses Chinese and English documents and PDFs, and MiniCPM-OCR Jev scores whether each OCR result region is reliable.
summary.what_it_does: MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (1.3B) is a text-centric document parsing model that handles text, tables, formulas, charts, seals, and structured information extraction for Chinese and English documents and PDFs, including scans, photographs, curved and skewed pages, and recaptured documents. Its outputs are described as Markdown or JSON. MiniCPM-OCR Jev is a separate 2B model that takes an image and its OCR result and returns a quality score from 0 to 1 for text, formulas, and tables, to help select reliable results and locate content needing review. The README says both models work with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and Ollama, and that 1.0 offers a pip SDK, a full-featured API, fine-tuning tutorials (LLaMA-Factory, Swift), and quantized weights (BF16, GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ). Performance claims (such as SOTA scores on OmniDocBench and OCRBench v2) are the authors' own reported results.
use_cases: parse scanned Chinese or English documents into Markdown
extract text and tables from photographs of pages
convert PDFs to structured JSON or Markdown
score which OCR results are reliable and need human review
how_to_run: Read the MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 deployment tutorial for local setup (linked from the README; no commands given in the README itself)
Or send the MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 skill instruction to a coding agent, or use ./docs/SKILL_en.md if the repo is cloned
Use the Free API for hosted MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 recognition (example linked in the README)
Install the pip SDK for application integration (per the README; exact command is in the linked guides)
notable: MiniCPM-OCR Jev gives region-level correctness scores, flagging problematic regions regardless of which OCR model produced the parse
DSpark decoding acceleration is claimed to improve end-to-end efficiency by 55%
Supports vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and Ollama from day one, with quantized versions at release
Targets hard capture conditions such as curved pages, photographs, and recaptured documents
caveats: Performance and throughput figures are self-reported by the authors and tied to specific benchmarks and test settings
MiniCPM-OCR Jev API example is marked 'coming soon' in the README
Some deployment and usage details are only in linked guides, not in the README itself
